readings.title: Hannah's Vow and Peace
readings.text: [1 Samuel 1:9] And Ḥannah rose up after eating and drinking in Shiloh. And Ĕli the priest was sitting on the seat by the doorpost of the Hĕykal of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [10] And she was bitter in soul, and prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and wept greatly. [11] And she made a vow and said, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, if <dn>You</dn> would indeed look on the affliction of <dn>Your</dn> female servant and remember me, and not forget <dn>Your</dn> female servant, but shall give <dn>Your</dn> female servant a male child, then I shall give him to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> all the days of his life, and no razor shall come upon his head.” [12] And it came to be, as she continued praying before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that Ĕli watched her mouth. [13] Now Ḥannah spoke in her heart, only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard. And Ĕli thought she was drunk. [14] And Ĕli said to her, “How long are you going to be drunk? Put away your wine from you!” [15] And Ḥannah answered and said, “No, my master, I am a woman hard in spirit. I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but I poured out my soul before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [16] “Do not take your female servant for a daughter of Beliyaʽal, for out of the abundance of my complaint and grief I have spoken until now.” [17] And Ĕli answered and said, “Go in peace, and the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl give you your petition which you have asked of <dn>Him</dn>.” [18] And she said, “Let your female servant find favor in your eyes.” And the woman went her way and ate, and her face was no longer sad.

readings.title: The Birth and Dedication of Samuel
readings.text: [1 Samuel 1:19] And they rose early in the morning and worshipped before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and returned and came to their house at Ramah. And Elqanah knew Ḥannah his wife, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> remembered her. [20] And it came to be, at the turn of days, that Ḥannah conceived and bore a son, and called his name Shemu’ĕl, “Because I have asked <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for him.” [21] And the man Elqanah and all his house went up to slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> the yearly slaughtering and his vow. [22] But Ḥannah did not go up, for she said to her husband, “Not until the child is weaned, then I shall take him, and he shall appear before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and remain there forever.” [23] And Elqanah her husband said to her, “Do what is good in your eyes. Remain until you have weaned him. Only, let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> establish <dn>His</dn> word.” And the woman remained and nursed her son until she had weaned him. [24] And when she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with three bulls, and one ĕphah of flour, and a skin of wine, and brought him to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in Shiloh. And the child was young. [25] And they slaughtered the bull, and brought the child to Ĕli. [26] And she said, “O my master! As your soul lives, my master, I am the woman who stood by you here, praying to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [27] “I prayed for this child, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has granted me my petition which I asked of <dn>Him</dn>. [28] “Therefore I also have lent him to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. All the days that he lives he shall be lent to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” And he worshipped there before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: Hannah's Prayer of Exaltation
readings.text: [1 Samuel 2:1] And Ḥannah prayed and said, “My heart rejoices in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, my horn is exalted in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. My mouth is opened wide over my enemies, for I rejoice in <dn>Your</dn> deliverance. [2] “There is no one set-apart like <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for there is no one besides <dn>You</dn>, and there is no Rock like our <dn>Elohim</dn>. [3] “Do not multiply words so proudly, proudly; let no arrogance come from your mouth, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is an <dn>Ěl</dn> of knowledge, and by <dn>Him</dn> deeds are weighed. [4] “Bows of the mighty are broken, and those who stumbled are girded with strength. [5] “The satisfied have hired themselves out for bread, and the hungry have ceased. Even the barren has borne seven, and she who has many children pines away. [6] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> puts to death and makes alive, <dn>He</dn> brings down to She’ol and raises up. [7] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> makes poor and makes rich, <dn>He</dn> brings low and lifts up. [8] “<dn>He</dn> raises the poor from the dust, <dn>He</dn> lifts the needy from the dunghill, to sit with princes, and make them inherit a throne of esteem. For the supports of the earth belong to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> has set the world upon them. [9] “<dn>He</dn> guards the feet of <dn>His</dn> kind ones, but the wrong are silent in darkness, for man does not become mighty by power. [10] “Those who strive with <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> are beaten down, <dn>He</dn> thunders against them in the heavens. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> judges the ends of the earth, and gives strength to <dn>His</dn> sovereign, and exalts the horn of <dn>His</dn> anointed.” [11] And Elqanah went to Ramah to his house. And the child served <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> before Ĕli the priest.

readings.title: The Wicked Sons of Eli
readings.text: [1 Samuel 2:12] Now the sons of Ĕli were sons of Beliyaʽal, they did not know <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [13] And the ruling of the priests with the people was, that when any man slaughtered a slaughtering, the priest’s servant came with a three-pronged flesh-hook in his hand while the meat was cooking, [14] and he struck it into the pan, or kettle, or caldron, or pot. Whatever the flesh-hook brought up, the priest took for himself. This they did in Shiloh to all Yisra’ĕl who came there. [15] Also, before they burned the fat, the priest’s servant came and said to the man who slaughtered, “Give meat for roasting to the priest, for he does not accept cooked meat from you, but raw.” [16] And if the man said to him, “Let them certainly burn the fat first, and then take as much as your being desires,” he would then answer him, “No, but give it now. And if not, I take it by force.” [17] And the sin of the young men was very great before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for men despised the offering of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [18] But Shemu’ĕl served before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, as a child, wearing a linen shoulder garment. [19] And his mother used to make him a small robe, and bring it to him year by year when she came up with her husband to slaughter the yearly slaughtering. [20] And Ĕli would bless Elqanah and his wife, and say, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> give you offspring from this woman for the loan that was lent to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” And they would go to their own home. [21] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> visited Ḥannah, so that she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. And the young Shemu’ĕl grew before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [22] And Ĕli was very old, and heard all that his sons did to all Yisra’ĕl, and how they lay with the women who assembled at the door of the Tent of Meeting. [23] And he said to them, “Why do you do such deeds as these? For I hear of your evil deeds from all the people. [24] “No, my sons! For it is not a good report that I hear. You make <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>’s people transgress. [25] “If one man sins against another, <dn>Elohim</dn> shall judge him. But if a man sins against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who shall pray for him?” But they did not listen to the voice of their father, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> desired to put them to death. [26] And the young Shemu’ĕl grew in stature, and in favor both with <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and men.

readings.title: Prophecy Against the House of Eli
readings.text: [1 Samuel 2:27] And a man of <dn>Elohim</dn> came to Ĕli and said to him, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Did <dn>I</dn> not clearly reveal <dn>Myself</dn> to the house of your father when they were in Mitsrayim in Pharaoh’s house?</dq> [28] <dq>‘And did <dn>I</dn> not choose him out of all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl to be <dn>My</dn> priest, to offer upon <dn>My</dn> slaughter-place, to burn incense, and to wear an ephod before <dn>Me</dn>? And did <dn>I</dn> not give to the house of your father all the fire offerings of the children of Yisra’ĕl?</dq> [29] <dq>‘Why do you kick at <dn>My</dn> slaughtering and <dn>My</dn> offering which <dn>I</dn> have commanded in <dn>My</dn> dwelling place, and esteem your sons above <dn>Me</dn>, to make yourselves fat with the best of all the offerings of Yisra’ĕl <dn>My</dn> people?’</dq> [30] “Therefore <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl says, <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> said indeed that your house and the house of your father would walk before <dn>Me</dn> forever.’</dq> But now <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> says, <dq>‘Far be it from <dn>Me</dn>. For those who esteem <dn>Me</dn> <dn>I</dn> esteem, and those who despise <dn>Me</dn> are lightly esteemed.</dq> [31] <dq>‘See, the days are coming that <dn>I</dn> shall cut off your arm and the arm of your father’s house, so that there is not an old man in your house.</dq> [32] <dq>‘And you shall see an enemy in <dn>My</dn> dwelling place, despite all the good which is done for Yisra’ĕl. And there shall not be an old man in your house forever.</dq> [33] <dq>‘But any of your men whom <dn>I</dn> do not cut off from <dn>My</dn> slaughter-place is to consume your eyes and to grieve your being. And all the increase of your house shall die as men.</dq> [34] <dq>‘And this is the sign to you that comes upon your two sons, on Ḥophni and Pineḥas: in one day they shall die, both of them.</dq> [35] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall raise up for <dn>Myself</dn> a trustworthy priest who does according to what is in <dn>My</dn> heart and in <dn>My</dn> being. And <dn>I</dn> shall build him a steadfast house, and he shall walk before <dn>My</dn> anointed forever.</dq> [36] <dq>‘And it shall be that everyone who is left in your house shall come and bow down to him for a piece of silver and a cake of bread, and say, “Please put me in one of the priestly offices to eat a piece of bread.” ’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Call of Samuel
readings.text: [1 Samuel 3:1] And the young Shemu’ĕl served <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> before Ĕli. And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was rare in those days, no vision breaking forth. [2] And it came to be in that day, while Ĕli was lying down in his place, and when his eyes had begun to grow dim – he was unable to see – [3] and before the lamp of <dn>Elohim</dn> went out in the Hĕykal of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> where the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> was, and while Shemu’ĕl was lying down, [4] that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> called Shemu’ĕl. And he answered, “Here I am!” [5] And he ran to Ĕli and said, “Here I am, for you called me.” And he said, “I did not call. Go back, lie down.” And he went and lay down. [6] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> called yet again, “Shemu’ĕl!” And Shemu’ĕl rose up and went to Ĕli, and said, “Here I am, for you called me.” And he answered, “I did not call, my son. Go back, lie down.” [7] Now Shemu’ĕl did not yet know <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, nor was the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> yet revealed to him. [8] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> called Shemu’ĕl again the third time. And he rose up and went to Ĕli, and said, “Here I am, for you did call me.” Then Ĕli understood that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was calling the youth. [9] So Ĕli said to Shemu’ĕl, “Go, lie down. And it shall be, if <dn>He</dn> calls you, that you say, ‘Speak, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>Your</dn> servant hears.’ ” And Shemu’ĕl went and lay down in his place. [10] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came and stood and called as at other times, “Shemu’ĕl! Shemu’ĕl!” And Shemu’ĕl answered, “Speak, for <dn>Your</dn> servant hears.” [11] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Shemu’ĕl, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am doing a deed in Yisra’ĕl, at which both ears of everyone who hears it shall tingle.</dq> [12] <dq>“In that day <dn>I</dn> establish against Ĕli all that <dn>I</dn> have spoken concerning his house, from beginning to end.</dq> [13] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> have declared to him that <dn>I</dn> am judging his house forever for the crookedness which he knew, because his sons cursed <dn>Elohim</dn>, and he did not rebuke them.</dq> [14] <dq>“And therefore <dn>I</dn> have sworn to the house of Ĕli that the crookedness of Ĕli’s house is not covered by slaughtering or grain offering forever.”</dq>

readings.title: Samuel Established as Prophet
readings.text: [1 Samuel 3:15] And Shemu’ĕl lay down until morning, and opened the doors of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And Shemu’ĕl was afraid to report the vision to Ĕli. [16] Then Ĕli called Shemu’ĕl and said, “Shemu’ĕl, my son!” And he answered, “Here I am.” [17] And he said, “What is the word that <dn>He</dn> spoke to you? Please do not hide it from me. <dn>Elohim</dn> do so to you, and more also, if you hide anything from me of all the words that <dn>He</dn> spoke to you.” [18] And Shemu’ĕl reported to him all the words, and hid nothing from him. And he said, “It is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Let <dn>Him</dn> do what is good in <dn>His</dn> eyes.” [19] And Shemu’ĕl grew, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was with him and let none of <dn>his</dn> words fall to the ground. [20] And all Yisra’ĕl from Dan to Be’ĕrsheḇa knew that Shemu’ĕl was established as a prophet of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [21] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> continued to appear in Shiloh, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> revealed <dn>Himself</dn> to Shemu’ĕl in Shiloh by the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [1 Samuel 4:1a] And the word of Shemu’ĕl came to all Yisra’ĕl.

readings.title: The Ark Taken by Philistines
readings.text: [1 Samuel 4:1b] And Yisra’ĕl went out to battle against the Philistines, and encamped beside Eḇen Haʽĕzer. And the Philistines encamped in Aphĕq. [2] And the Philistines put themselves in battle array against Yisra’ĕl. And when they joined battle, Yisra’ĕl was smitten before the Philistines, who killed about four thousand men of the army in the field. [3] And when the people had come into the camp, the elders of Yisra’ĕl said, “Why has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> smitten us today before the Philistines? Let us bring the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> from Shiloh to us, so that <dn>He</dn> comes into our midst and saves us from the hand of our enemies.” [4] And the people sent to Shiloh, and they brought from there the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, dwelling between the keruḇim. And the two sons of Ĕli, Ḥophni and Pineḥas, were there with the ark of the covenant of <dn>Elohim</dn>. [5] And when the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came into the camp, all Yisra’ĕl shouted with a great shout, so that the earth shook. [6] And when the Philistines heard the noise of the shout, they said, “What is the noise of this great shout in the camp of the Iḇrim?” And they knew that the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had come into the camp. [7] And the Philistines were afraid, for they said, “<dn>Elohim</dn> has come into the camp!” And they said, “Woe to us! For such a thing has never happened before. [8] “Woe to us! Who shall deliver us from the hand of these mighty <dn>Elohim</dn>? These are the <dn>Elohim</dn> who smote the Mitsrites with all the plagues in the wilderness. [9] “Be strong and be men, O Philistines, lest you serve the Iḇrim as they have served you. Be men and fight!” [10] And the Philistines fought, and Yisra’ĕl was smitten, and every man fled to his tent. And the slaughter was very great, and there fell of Yisra’ĕl thirty thousand foot soldiers. [11] And the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> was taken, and the two sons of Ĕli, Ḥophni and Pineḥas, died.
